title: Agentic RAG — Retrieval as a Tool

content.goal: Wrap retrieval as a tool the agent can call.
content.why: In basic RAG, retrieval is a fixed pipeline. In agentic RAG, retrieval becomes a TOOL the agent chooses to use — deciding WHEN and WHAT to search. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 11, section 11.6.)
content.verify: The file saves. ATLAS now has search_docs alongside its other tools — retrieval is a capability the agent can reach for, not a fixed step.

content.goal: Update the system prompt so the agent grounds and cites when it uses search_docs.
content.why: The grounding discipline still applies — answer only from retrieved context and cite sources — but now the agent decides when to retrieve. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 11, section 11.4.)
content.code:
ATLAS_SYSTEM = (
    "You are ATLAS. Think, then use tools when they help; do not guess facts you can look up. "
    "When you use search_docs, answer using ONLY the returned passages and cite their source. "
    "If the documents do not contain the answer, say so. "
    "When you have enough to answer, give a final answer and stop."
)
# Pass ATLAS_SYSTEM as the system message in run_agent().
content.verify: The file saves. The agent's instructions now combine tool-use guidance with the grounding rule.

content.goal: Ask a question that makes the agent CHOOSE to retrieve.
content.why: Agentic RAG shines on questions where the agent decides retrieval is needed — versus answering directly. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 11, section 11.6.)
content.code:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(run_agent("According to my notes, what are the office hours?"))
content.verify: In the trace you see ATLAS call search_docs, receive passages, then answer with a citation. Ask a general-knowledge question instead ("what is 2+2?") and it should answer WITHOUT retrieving — that judgment is the point of agentic RAG.
content.troubleshoot: If it retrieves for everything, tighten the tool description ("only for the user's own documents"). If it never retrieves, make the description clearer about when to use it.

content.goal: Enable MULTI-HOP retrieval — search, read, then search again with a refined query.
content.why: The loop lets the agent realize it needs more, and search again — something a fixed pipeline cannot do. (Learned in Phase 9, Ch 11, section 11.6, and Ch 7.)
content.verify: The trace shows TWO search_docs calls — the second query built from what the first returned. That is multi-hop retrieval, the loop of Chapter 7 applied to search.
content.troubleshoot: If it stops after one search, remind it in the goal that it may search more than once. Your step limit (Unit 5) still bounds the total work.

content.goal: CHECKPOINT — retrieval is now an agent capability.
content.why: You have turned a fixed RAG pipeline into agentic RAG — the most common powerful real-world pattern.
content.verify: All true — search_docs is a tool; the agent decides when to use it; answers from documents are grounded and cited; multi-hop questions trigger more than one search; general questions skip retrieval. Next unit refactors ATLAS onto a framework and compares it to your raw build.
